review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner; self-review, not independent approval
review.decision: Close inherited Chat auth-denial ordering and Jump/paging cancellation in a separate candidate before release
review.notes: Full independent REVIEW1159 read and SHA-verified; current base7d1366 hook is exact blob6edc from S834/175/176, and current ChatView callbacks retain both reviewed conditions. Preserve existing LCL-003/004 continuity, identity/cursor semantics, timeouts and all old test assertions. New tests mount actual React hook/ChatView with synthetic deferred GtmuxClient reads and normal RN native mocks; no extracted callback toy, real session, device or pixel claim. Denial must bind the currently rendered snapshot at failure, not the request-start array. Jump always invalidates active pagination, leaves intentional same-reader cached history policy intact, and cancels stale window continuations/offset anchors; new valid reads still work. Keep source P1 PR1855/Q frozen; this follows fresh main7d1366 after independent approval and normal merge. UI failure assertions must be semantic, not compile/mock/setup failure; save old-red/source and new-green snapshots. No new dependencies, transport fallback, weaker auth, forced input, broader mount count or shortened original budgets. Follow-up review before adding CPG-004: an already observed array must not count as a post-denial authorized snapshot merely because its reference differs from the most recent one. Scope weak reference-generation labels to the reader and retire all observed generations through failure; this also avoids allowing an older render after refusal. Keep no additional turn payload cache and no new server authority.

cases.description: Current snapshot retires when a pending earlier-page read is refused after recent polling changed
cases.setup: Actual React useChatHistory/ChatView, recent A then B while a synthetic deferred page is pending; ApiError401/403 and normal failure/identity controls.
cases.action: Reject the old page after recent B is rendered, inspect turns/refusal/error, then supply a subsequent fresh recent snapshot; also reject an old reader after target change.
cases.expected: At refusal the current content is retired, denied/failed visible and loading false; only subsequent fresh source data for the same reader restores content, without resurrecting cached prefix. Network errors retain current content; stale reader errors never erase a new reader.

cases.description: Jump supersedes pending pages in continuous and disconnected history
cases.setup: Actual mounted hook and ChatView with controlled noncooperative history promise, continuous20-turn recent window and disconnected-tail control; no animation/frame completion before late result.
cases.action: Start earlier page, Jump to latest, resolve late page, inspect AbortSignal/window/error/prepend callback and issue a later legitimate page.
cases.expected: Old request is invalidated, loading resets, late page produces no insertion/window enlargement/compensation, latest20-turn intent remains. New paging still works with authoritative cursor; existing disconnected behavior and20-turn-per-page mounting remain.

cases.description: Jump retires pending scroll anchors and UI continuation without disabling normal history
cases.setup: Actual ChatView and observed RN ScrollView mock imperative methods; accepted earlier page has an unconsumed content-size anchor.
cases.action: Jump before the delayed content-size callback or a late page continuation, then emit content size and selected next reader controls.
cases.expected: No obsolete history-offset scrollTo or window re-expansion after Jump; current follow-tail behavior remains and new legitimate paging can insert normally. These are actual React/imperative-call observations, not device pixel/animation certification.

cases.description: Revisiting an already observed snapshot never lifts a refusal
cases.setup: Actual React hook has observed arrays A and B; page starts and is refused while B remains current, with an initial same-reference refusal control.
cases.action: After refusal, render old A and B again, then supply a genuinely fresh array C for the same reader.
cases.expected: Both previously observed snapshots stay retired and failed/denied remain visible; only C restores content. Reader-local weak generation metadata must not turn an old cached array into a new authorization or retain turn payloads.
